meta.how_to_use: Answer the priority-1 questions first: until Q01-Q03 are answered, no route can be selected and no cost figure is a plan. Each question states what is already known, why the gap blocks a decision, and how to close it.

questions.blocks: Everything: which rule set applies at all
questions.question: Are you still a PRC citizen with a PRC resident identity card, or only a U.S. passport holder (with or without a PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID)?
questions.why: PBOC Decree [2006] No.3 Art. 37 splits all individual FX business into 境内个人 (PRC citizens holding a PRC ID/serviceman/police certificate) and 境外个人 (non-Chinese passports, HK/Macao/Taiwan travel-permit holders, stateless persons). The annual USD 50,000 purchase quota is written for 境内个人; a 境外个人 gets a quota only with a Foreign Permanent Resident ID. State Council Regulation 532 Art. 52(2) adds a second, different test — Chinese citizen OR a foreigner continuously resident in the PRC for one full year. The two tests are not the same, and which one the bank applies changes the documents you must produce.
questions.we_have: The instruction 'as a US citizen'. That is not enough: dual status is common and the two definitions diverge.
questions.how_to_find: Read the identity-document field the bank used when it opened the account (the account category is recorded per PBOC Decree Art. 28). Ask the bank in writing: 'Is this account held as 境内个人 or 境外个人, and under which article?' Check whether a Foreign Permanent Resident ID exists.
questions.if_unknown: Cannot choose between routes 1 and 3. Every cost table here is computed for BOTH statuses, and the eligibility column says which is available.

questions.blocks: Whether any lawful route exists; whether tax is owed
questions.question: What is the documented source of this CNY balance — salary, business income, sale of property, inheritance, gift, or accumulated savings — and is there a paper trail for each tranche?
questions.why: Regulation 532 Art. 12 requires a real, lawful transaction basis for every current-account FX receipt and payment, and the bank must reasonably review the documents. 汇发[2007]1号 Art. 10 and 13 require named source evidence (employment contract and income proof, tax record, inheritance documents, property-sale documents). Without a source you cannot use a current-account route at all, and no fee comparison matters.
questions.we_have: Nothing. The balance's composition is unknown.
questions.how_to_find: Request from the bank: 12 months of statements plus the historical credit entries; from the tax authority: the personal income tax record (个人所得税纳税记录) via the provincial e-tax bureau or app; from any employer: contracts, payslips, withholding statements.
questions.if_unknown: Route 1/2 unproven. The only realistic routes become route 5 (emigrant transfer, if household registration is cancelled) or route 6 (inheritance). Both are capital-account routes with SAFE approval, staged over two years (route 5).

questions.blocks: Whether a China tax is actually owed on the income
questions.question: Has PRC individual income tax been assessed and paid on the income that produced this balance — and can you obtain the 完税证明 or 个人所得税纳税记录?
questions.why: PRC IIT Law Art. 3 taxes the income (3%-45% comprehensive; 20% on interest, dividends, rent and property transfer). The FX rules do not add a tax on conversion; they ask for evidence of the source, and Announcement 2013 No. 40 Art. 1 requires tax recordal for single outward payments above USD 50,000. Whether any tax is due depends on the income, not on the transfer.
questions.we_have: Unknown. Prior sections wrote '0% conversion tax' and, in places, '0% extra PRC tax if IIT was already withheld' — an assumption, not a fact.
questions.how_to_find: Log in to the provincial e-tax bureau (自然人电子税务局) and download the personal tax record; or ask the withholding employer/agent for the withholding statement. Compare the record's total income with the balance.
questions.if_unknown: Cannot tell whether the 'considerable tax' the bank mentioned is (a) tax already owed on the income, (b) a recordal step, or (c) a fee. This is exactly the ambiguity in the original question.

questions.blocks: Which of the documented routes is usable
questions.question: What did the bank actually say, in writing — which document did it request, and under which rule did it refuse?
questions.why: 'A requested tax certificate', 'an actual tax assessment', 'an FX eligibility question' and 'a transfer fee' have completely different fixes. Announcement 2013 No. 40 Art. 6 says the tax authority need not examine the tax position at recordal. If the bank is asking for a 备案表 number, that is a free online filing, not a tax.
questions.we_have: A paraphrase ('without paying a considerable amount of taxes'). No document reference.
questions.how_to_find: Ask for the refusal in writing, naming: the tax type (if any), taxpayer, period, base, amount and legal basis; or the exact document list. Send the question through the bank's complaint channel so there is a record.
questions.if_unknown: The cost model is being applied to a problem that may be a paperwork problem, not a money problem.

questions.question: What is your U.S. tax basis in the CNY — the USD value when each tranche was received — and is your other U.S. taxable income in 2026 known?
questions.why: 26 U.S.C. § 988(c)(1)(C) treats disposing of foreign currency as a section 988 transaction. For a personal transaction, § 988(e)(2) excludes the gain unless it exceeds USD 200; above that, § 988(a)(1)(A) makes it ordinary income unless an election applies. The size of the gain is (proceeds − basis), and the rate depends on your other income (Rev. Proc. 2025-32).
questions.we_have: Nothing. No basis, no other income, no filing status.
questions.how_to_find: Reconstruct the USD value of each deposit at the spot rate on the day received (IRS accepts any consistently applied posted rate). Keep the statements; then compare with the conversion date.
questions.if_unknown: The U.S. layer is shown as a labelled illustration across assumptions, never as your liability.

questions.blocks: U.S. reporting exposure (which dwarfs the fees)
questions.question: Have you filed FBAR (FinCEN 114) and, if thresholds are met, Form 8938 for the years this account existed?
questions.why: A U.S. person must file an FBAR where aggregate foreign accounts exceeded USD 10,000 at any time in the year, and 8938 at USD 50,000/75,000 (single, in the U.S.) or USD 100,000/150,000 (MFJ, in the U.S.). Non-willful FBAR maxima are USD 16,536 per violation and willful maxima USD 165,353 (penalties assessed on or after 17 Jan 2025).
questions.we_have: Nothing. Prior sessions flagged this as unknown too.
questions.how_to_find: Check prior returns and the FinCEN BSA e-filing history. If unfiled, get advice on delinquent filing or the Streamlined procedures before moving money — the answer changes the sequencing, not just the cost.
questions.if_unknown: A transfer that creates a visible USD inflow without the filings in place is the scenario in which the largest numbers in this project apply. Fees of 0.2% are irrelevant next to a USD 165,353 maximum.

questions.question: Where is your tax home and residency in 2026 — the U.S., mainland China, or split — and are you claiming the foreign earned income exclusion or foreign tax credit?
questions.why: The 1984 U.S.-PRC treaty and the § 911 exclusion depend on residency and tax home; § 988(a)(3)(B) sets the source of currency gain by reference to the taxpayer's tax home. Filing status also changes the 8938 thresholds and the bracket the gain lands in.
questions.how_to_find: Determine days present and tax home; if claiming § 911, the Form 2555 qualification must be documented. Compare with the treaty's saving clause before assuming treaty relief.
questions.if_unknown: Treaty and exclusion results are not asserted anywhere in this section; the illustrations show the U.S. statutory layer only.

questions.question: Do you need the whole amount in one movement, and what is the actual deadline?
questions.why: Route 5 (emigrant transfer) is expressly staged: half first, then up to half of the remainder after one year, the rest after two years (Announcement 2004 No. 16 Art. 6). The annual facilitation quota resets on 1 January and unused quota does not carry over.
questions.we_have: An amount range (USD 10,000-400,000) but no deadline or liquidity need.
questions.how_to_find: State the cash need and date. If a bank offers staging, get the schedule in writing.
questions.if_unknown: Cannot compare a one-off documented conversion against a two-year capital-account programme on a like-for-like basis.

questions.question: What is the bank's executable all-in quote today: applied CNY/USD rate, sender fee, cable, correspondent deduction and receiving-bank charge?
questions.why: Every rate board reviewed carries a disclaimer that it is for reference and the transaction rate prevails. BOC's board says so explicitly; HSBC's says rates may change without notice. HSBC's tariff note 7 excludes other institutions' charges.
questions.we_have: Reference boards only (BOC 6.6630/6.6911; CMB 6.66295/6.69199; HSBC 6.6411822/6.7079204) and published fee schedules.
questions.how_to_find: Ask for a written quote for the exact amount and date, plus the intermediary/correspondent bank's deduction and the receiving bank's inward fee.
questions.if_unknown: Every total in this project is a lower bound on a reference rate, labelled as such.

questions.blocks: Whether a third-country step is worth anything
questions.question: Do you have a lawful need and a compliant account in Hong Kong or elsewhere that could receive the funds, and would that actually reduce the cost?
questions.why: Moving money to a third jurisdiction does not remove the PRC documentation requirement at the point of purchase, and it adds a second FX conversion and a second set of receiving fees. Nothing in the reviewed sources offers a lower-tax path for the same balance.
questions.we_have: Nothing. No third-country account is known to exist.
questions.how_to_find: Price it: PRC bank sell rate + wire + HK receiving fee + HK sell rate to USD. Compare with the direct quote from Q09.
questions.if_unknown: Third-country routing is listed in the methods table with its extra layers and left unpriced.

questions.question: Is any part of this balance realistically available as FX cash, and do you want to carry it?
questions.why: Carrying FX cash out is capped in practice: up to USD 5,000 needs no certificate, USD 5,000-10,000 needs a bank certificate, above USD 10,000 needs a SAFE certificate and is 'in principle' not allowed. RMB cash is capped at CNY 20,000 per person per trip. Entering the U.S. with more than USD 10,000 requires a FinCEN 105 report.
questions.we_have: No information about whether the balance can be withdrawn as cash at all.
questions.how_to_find: Ask the bank whether FX cash is available at the branch and in what denominations; confirm the reporting duty at the U.S. end before travelling.
questions.if_unknown: Cash is listed, costed at the cash spread where published, and marked impractical for the amounts in question.

questions.blocks: Whether the 'penalty' is avoidable at all
questions.question: Is the shortfall the bank describes a currency-conversion loss (spread), a tax on income, or a compliance cost — and has anyone put a number on each?
questions.why: The seven layers are separable and only some are avoidable: spread (shoppable), wire/cable/correspondent fees (partly shoppable), tax recordal (free), PRC income tax (fixed by the income, not the transfer), U.S. currency gain (usually under USD 200), U.S. reporting (a filing duty), and penalties for unlawful routes (avoidable only by not using them).
questions.how_to_find: Use the Penalties page: it prices each layer at each USD 10,000 step and marks which are avoidable.
questions.if_unknown: The cost tables still give the number for every layer that can be computed from published inputs.

questions.question: Which bank actually holds the account, and what is that bank's own current fee schedule?
questions.why: This session captured fee schedules for BOC and HSBC China and rate boards for BOC, CMB and HSBC. ICBC's board and feed returned no data to this session and CMB's remittance fee schedule was not captured, so those cells are blank rather than copied from an earlier snapshot.
questions.we_have: Partial. Three live rate boards, two fee schedules.
questions.how_to_find: Name the bank and branch; pull its posted personal tariff (服务价目表) and the branch's own posted rates.
questions.if_unknown: Blank cells stay blank and are listed on the Flagged for Review page.

questions.question: Has anyone independent — a PRC-qualified tax adviser or the bank's compliance desk — confirmed the route before money moves?
questions.why: This project is document review. It is not advice, no bank was contacted, and no account-specific fact was entered. The published rules are conditional and applied by a branch officer to a specific file.
questions.how_to_find: Take this dashboard's Questions page and the bank's written answer from Q04 to a PRC-qualified adviser; ask them to confirm the route and the document list in writing.
questions.if_unknown: Nothing here should be executed on its own.
